mfg1-mechanical-lesson-050.title: Read specific gravity as a density ratio and keep units distinct
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-050.objective: Distinguish the reference for specific gravity from density units, and compare values under the same conditions.

paragraphs.title: Check the reference
paragraphs.text: Specific gravity is treated as the ratio to the density of a reference substance. This source uses water at 4°C, with specific gravity 1, as the reference for solids and liquids. Distinguish this ratio from density values carrying units such as g/cm³. Records with different references or temperatures are not identical merely because their numbers look alike.

paragraphs.title: Calculate an equal-volume comparison
paragraphs.text: In a paper example, the masses of equal volumes of a specimen and reference water are specified as 84 g and 30 g. Their ratio is 84÷30=2.8. This differs from simply dividing the masses of objects with different volumes. These numbers are for learning, not inspection results certifying a material grade at work.

paragraphs.title: Copy numbers from a material table
paragraphs.text: The source gives metal examples including aluminum 2.68 and iron 7.87. Alloys and conditions can differ, so do not replace these with density values from another source without authorization. When discussing a lighter part, check required strength, shape, temperature and material approval as well as specific gravity.

terms.meaning: A ratio to the density of a reference substance.
The substance used as the basis of comparison.
Having no unit because it is a ratio of quantities of the same kind.
Having the same volume.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-050.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Calculate ratios from two sets of equal-volume masses. Separate the record fields for density, specific gravity and reference temperature.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not identify an unknown material as the specified grade and machine it on the basis of specific gravity alone.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-050.summary: Specific gravity is a ratio with a reference. Keep it distinct from density units and compare under matching conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-051.title: Choose how to position a steel rule and a protractor
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-051.objective: Separate length and angle measurement targets, and check end faces, reference faces and viewing direction.

paragraphs.title: Read length with a steel rule
paragraphs.text: A steel rule measures length. Align the end of the object with the reference position and read the scale from directly in front. Check chipped ends or dirty graduations. Do not assume it can guarantee precision tolerances merely because it is read like a paper ruler. Select the instrument specified by the requirement.

paragraphs.title: An angle is a relationship between two faces
paragraphs.text: A protractor generally combines a graduated angle plate with a blade. Place the base and blade against the two planes whose angle is required, then read the scale. If one side is lifted or touches a different face, a readable number is still not the target angle.

paragraphs.title: Ask about instrument selection
paragraphs.text: Separate a request for an end length from a request for the angle of a sloping face. If the two reference faces are unclear, show the drawing and ask. Do not substitute an easier-to-see face. Record the instrument, target, contact faces and unit.

terms.meaning: An instrument that reads length from graduations.
The part carrying angle graduations.
The bar-shaped part placed against the measured face.
A face where the instrument and target touch.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-051.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Draw one length and one angle. Use colors to distinguish the reference and the two contact faces.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not place an instrument against moving parts. Watch sharp edges and use the specified measurement procedure.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-051.summary: Check the correct target and contact, as well as a readable scale.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-052.title: Separate the references of height gauges and depth gauges
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-052.objective: Explain the reference face, movement direction and scale increment for height and depth measurements.

paragraphs.title: The surface plate is the height reference
paragraphs.text: A height gauge is used on a surface plate to measure heights from that plane. Check that the measuring contact moves perpendicular to the reference face, and that the gauge base and plate have no foreign matter. Do not treat a tilted support as the same reference.

paragraphs.title: Depth starts from the upper reference face
paragraphs.text: A depth gauge measures depth from a reference face. Seat it stably against that face and check that the measuring face reaches the target correctly. If it has not reached the bottom of a groove, do not record a value chosen to match the drawing depth.

paragraphs.title: Check the increment for each instrument
paragraphs.text: Analog and digital displays are available. The source shows vernier examples with scale increments of 0.05 mm or 0.02 mm; this does not apply to every instrument. Match instrument specifications, zero or datum setting, target location and temperature conditions before comparing results.

terms.meaning: An instrument measuring heights from a surface plate.
An instrument measuring depth from a reference face.
A flat platform providing a reference for measurement and similar work.
The point used as the basis for setting a value.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-052.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Mark separate reference faces for the height of a stepped part and its hole depth. Make an example record for a measurement not yet confirmed.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not force a measuring contact into place. Protect precision surfaces and follow the instrument procedure.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-052.summary: Height and depth use different reference faces. Record the specifications and contact for each instrument.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-053.title: Check safety responsibilities and everyday communication
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-053.objective: Identify the workplace safety and health organization and contact persons, and distinguish greetings from hazard reports.

paragraphs.title: Do not leave everything to one person
paragraphs.text: The source describes three aspects of occupational safety and health: standards for preventing harm, a system of responsibilities, and voluntary activities. Both the company and workers have roles. Naming a responsible person alone does not remove a hazard. Check whom you should consult and the emergency communication route.

paragraphs.title: Know specialist roles
paragraphs.text: A safety and health committee discusses safety and health issues; safety managers, occupational physicians and others have specialist roles. Confirm specific establishment and appointment requirements at the workplace. This lesson does not determine legal applicability by itself. Direct health concerns to the designated contact as well.

paragraphs.title: Greetings and reports serve different purposes
paragraphs.text: Morning greetings and words such as “work safely” help people cooperate. A nod alone, however, is not a report of a machine abnormality. Report the target, facts and actions clearly, and check that the other person understood.

terms.meaning: A system clarifying roles and the relationships for communication and decisions.
A specialist physician supporting workers’ health at the workplace.
The person or section receiving consultations and communications.
Speaking to someone to encourage attention or cooperation.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-053.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Draw an imaginary workplace contact chart. Connect greetings, abnormality reports and health consultations to suitable recipients.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not determine legal appointment or applicability conditions from this general lesson alone; confirm them with the responsible person.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-053.summary: Safety depends on both organization and daily actions. A greeting does not replace a report.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-054.title: Check training categories and the work you may perform
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-054.objective: Distinguish training on hiring or changing work from checking the qualifications and training needed for hazardous tasks.

paragraphs.title: Changed work requires new checks
paragraphs.text: When joining a workplace or moving to a new task, learn the hazards of machinery and raw materials, protective equipment, safety devices, procedures, pre-start checks, housekeeping and evacuation in an accident. Experience operating the previous machine does not mean a new machine can be operated under the same conditions.

paragraphs.title: Do not treat every qualification and course as the same
paragraphs.text: Forklifts, robot setting and maintenance, slinging and similar work require checking qualifications or training appropriate to the task and conditions. Do not describe one course as meeting every requirement. Confirm the requirements for the work and equipment with the responsible person. Reading the textbook or passing a mock exam does not replace workplace permission.

paragraphs.title: Match records to the permitted work
paragraphs.text: Know the training name, equipment covered, permitted activities and confirming person. If you learned operation but not internal adjustment, do not proceed to adjustment simply because it is the same machine. Stopping to ask about unfamiliar work is also part of learning safely.

terms.reading: やといいれじきょういく
terms.meaning: Training in necessary safety and health matters when starting employment.
A change in the work or conditions assigned.
A training category for specified dangerous or harmful work.
The work that is authorized and may be performed.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-054.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Imagine a transfer to a new machine. Make a table separating completed training, unconfirmed requirements and permitted work.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not begin work independently when the necessary qualifications, training or permission have not been confirmed.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-054.summary: Check the training type, target and scope. Study materials and workplace permission are different.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-055.title: Take near-miss reports beyond counting incidents
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-055.objective: Distinguish the educational meaning of Heinrich’s ratio from reporting facts and checking countermeasures.

paragraphs.title: No injury does not mean no information
paragraphs.text: A near miss is an event in which a danger was noticed even though no accident resulted. Examples include an object nearly falling or someone nearly slipping. Record the location, action and surrounding conditions as well as the outcome to help investigate causes. Do not omit a record just because nobody was hurt.

paragraphs.title: The ratio is not a fixed forecast
paragraphs.text: The source presents Heinrich’s concept as 1 serious accident,29 minor accidents and 300 near misses. This is an educational ratio encouraging attention to small warning signs, not a prediction formula that must produce the same numbers in every workplace. Consider the potential severity when responding.

paragraphs.title: Follow reporting through to verification
paragraphs.text: A cart wheel stopped at a step and the load tilted. Report the time, step location, loading arrangement and evacuation already taken. Share who will check each countermeasure. Counting reports alone does not mean the problem has been addressed; check for recurrence and other hazards after action.

terms.meaning: An event where danger was felt even though no accident occurred.
A change indicating a possible problem.
Relatively small in degree.
A similar problem happening again.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-055.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Use an imaginary event with no injury. Record facts, possible causes, measures and the person checking them separately.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not recreate a dangerous situation to prepare a report.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-055.summary: Use the ratio to encourage reports and verification of measures, rather than treating it as an inevitable forecast.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-056.title: Distinguish suspended-load hazards from fastening-tool hazards
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-056.objective: Explain falling loads, the effect of wire-rope angles, and the danger of forcing a threaded fastener.

paragraphs.title: Stay out from under suspended loads
paragraphs.text: A crane load can fall because of a wire-rope or attachment problem. Stay out from under the load and outside designated danger areas; follow access control and signals. Slinging and operation require the necessary qualifications, training and assigned scope. A nearby bystander must not independently start helping.

paragraphs.title: Angles change the forces
paragraphs.text: As the angle between wire ropes widens, the force on the ropes may increase even for the same load. Do not decide a safe angle or lifting method by appearance. Check the specified load, gear and plan. Do not calculate an actual lifting capacity from this lesson and change the arrangement independently.

paragraphs.title: Do not hammer a bolt that will not enter
paragraphs.text: Before using an impact wrench, check that the thread and part are compatible. If a bolt is difficult to insert, hammering its head can damage the threads. Do not force tightening. Follow the procedure to ask about the part number, alignment, foreign matter and damage.

terms.meaning: A load lifted by a crane or similar equipment.
Work attaching and removing the connections used to lift a load.
The helical part where threads engage.
A tool using an impact mechanism for tightening and related work.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-056.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Prepare separate notes for the exclusion area around a suspended load and a request to check a bolt that is difficult to insert.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not enter to steady a suspended load by hand. Do not change lifting or tightening conditions without authorization.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-056.summary: Treat suspended loads, rope angles and incompatible threads as distinct hazards to check.
